properties.name: Every cross-design read takes the other design by graph_id, and no registry server reads a host path (layer 1d)
properties.rationale: Anthony, 2026-10-11: "Let's prioritize getting 1b, 1c, 1d and 2 done of the views. Let's get that done before anything else." Layer 1d widens #720's resolver to the rest of the read family. The registry-path test, run first, found the hole wider than #720 had closed: nine path calls answered by reading files on the server's host, describe_designs naming a design stored at a host path, and import_graph importing a host file into the caller's design — all refused now on a registry server, stdio unchanged. Failing first 4 of 4; workspace 2,994 passed. Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019Xbw6PG9mXJiU2Sb421fnq
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: certify_preservation, merge_designs (other_graph_id + base_graph_id), analyze_alternatives (other_graph_ids), pair_designs and seam_report take the other design by graph_id through ReflowService::other_design (one guard at a time); their path or inline forms become optional and are refused together with a graph_id. One function, refuse_a_path_on_a_registry, refuses every path argument on a registry server: those reads plus fork_point, describe_designs, apply_merge, import_graph and external_dependency's design_export. Five toolsnaps re-blessed; the signature class test's fixture records apply_merge as refused on a registry; changelog fragment; AGENTS.md's cross-design section lists the tools and what stays open (export paths, wall_check's root, a stored design_export, the sync sidecar).
